description: the percentage distribution of commuters by transport mode in 2010, 2015, 2020 and 2025
overview: Car remained largest but fell by 22 percentage points. Bus use dipped then rose, while cycling increased throughout. Walking peaked in 2020. Distinguish percentage-point changes from proportional increases.

description: the percentages of residents using five community facilities in 2012, 2018 and 2024; residents could use more than one facility
table:
Facility | 2012 | 2018 | 2024
Library | 45% | 51% | 55%
Sports centre | 35% | 46% | 50%
Arts centre | 20% | 28% | 24%
Community garden | 10% | 18% | 32%
Swimming pool | 38% | 34% | 29%
overview: Library use remained highest. The garden overtook the arts centre and pool by 2024. Arts participation peaked in 2018; pool use fell throughout. Columns need not total 100% because residents could use several facilities.

description: household electricity use in 2010, 2018 and 2025, showing both its percentage distribution by purpose and average total annual consumption per household
table:
Measure | Unit | 2010 | 2018 | 2025
Heating | % of annual electricity | 45 | 38 | 30
Lighting | % of annual electricity | 20 | 14 | 10
Appliances | % of annual electricity | 25 | 33 | 40
Other | % of annual electricity | 10 | 15 | 20
Total annual consumption | kWh per household | 4000 | 4600 | 5200
overview: Heating and lighting lost share as total consumption rose. Appliances became largest. Heating fell in absolute terms (1800 to 1560 kWh) while appliances more than doubled (1000 to 2080 kWh). Do not confuse a share with a quantity.

description: the percentage distribution of commuters by distance travelled and the mean travel time for each group in 2015 and 2025
overview: The 2–5 km group became largest, replacing 5–10 km. The longest group kept its share but became faster; the shortest group grew but took longer. The only group to lose share also experienced a longer mean journey. Avoid deriving total commuter numbers from shares.

description: adult course enrolments and completion rates by subject in 2014 and 2024
table:
Subject | Enrolments 2014 | Enrolments 2024 | Completion 2014 | Completion 2024
Languages | 240 | 300 | 82% | 86%
Digital skills | 120 | 360 | 90% | 76%
Arts | 180 | 210 | 78% | 88%
Practical crafts | 160 | 230 | 85% | 84%
overview: All enrolment totals increased, most sharply in digital skills, which tripled. Its completion rate fell markedly while arts improved most and became highest. Do not assume the fastest-growing course had the best completion outcome.

description: the percentage distribution of municipal water use by sector in 2011, 2018 and 2025 and total daily water use
table:
Measure | Unit | 2011 | 2018 | 2025
Households | % of total | 50 | 48 | 45
Industry | % of total | 30 | 25 | 20
Public services | % of total | 15 | 17 | 20
Urban agriculture | % of total | 5 | 10 | 15
Total daily use | million litres | 40 | 44 | 50
overview: Households remained largest but lost share; their absolute use rose from 20 to 22.5 million litres daily. Industry fell in both share and quantity. Urban agriculture tripled its share and rose from 2 to 7.5 million litres. Distinguish proportional and absolute trends.
